source.title: Towards Understanding Multimodal Fine-Tuning: A Case Study into Spatial Features
source.authors: Lachin Naghashyar; Hunar Batra; Ashkan Khakzar; P. Torr; Ronald Clark; Christian Schroeder de Witt; Constantin Venhoff

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature analysis to a multimodal LLM setting and reports feature and ablation results relevant to whether dictionaries can recover behaviorally relevant features. It does not reproduce the toy-model superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper tests SAE feature identification and ablation in one VLM, relevant to V4. It does not test feature competition, superposition geometry as a capacity mechanism, polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical. Reconstruction values are reported as validation results; the reported feature-selection thresholds are choices used by the method, not standalone findings.
record.test_reason: The paper uses pretrained LLaMA-Scope SAEs, warm-started and fine-tuned on LLaVA-More activations, as a lens on multimodal fine-tuning. Its results are about which SAE features rotate or become spatially selective, and which heads drive them. It never asks whether the model holds sparse features in superposition or whether a dictionary can recover them; it presupposes this (Sec. 3.2). The FVU values validate the tool. The ablations are run on hand-picked top features and show their functional role, not a rate or extent of superposition. None of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that multimodal fine-tuning is structured and localizable at the feature level. Vision-preferring SAE features rotate during adaptation, and a subset encodes spatial relations. Ablating these features selectively hurts spatial reasoning, and a small group of mid-layer attention heads drives them. They call this an early step, limited to one model, and say further ablation and steering studies are needed.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses stage-wise SAE adaptation, feature selection, attribution patching, and decoder-direction ablation in a multimodal LLM; it does not use the original toy-network superposition experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature selection depends on visual-energy and decoder-cosine thresholds; the paper reports a threshold sweep and uses ϵ ≈ 10−3 and pcos ≈ 25%. The study also contrasts text-only, image-only, full-sequence, and random-initialized SAE training regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating single, hand-selected SAE decoder directions in LLaVA-More cuts VSR accuracy by about 6–16 points while general VQA changes by ≤1 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual SAE dictionary directions in a VLM backbone can be selectively causal for a specific capability (spatial reasoning).

fits_no_version.finding: Text-only SAEs stay aligned to the base LLM dictionary after multimodal fine-tuning. Image-only and full-sequence SAEs rotate strongly in shallow layers and realign later.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary features transfer across fine-tuning stages for text tokens but not for projector-driven image tokens.

record.problems: Only one model is tested. The authors say more detailed ablation and steering studies are needed and that other backbones and larger corpora are needed to assess generality. Ablation results are averaged over seeds, but seed counts and uncertainty estimates are not stated. Random-feature control effects are described as near zero or inconsistent, while several tabulated control values are not near zero.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's Table 1 reports additional individual-feature ablation values, but those six features are included in the more detailed Table 2 results; no duplicate rows were added. No other reported table rows were left out.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity transition, no feature geometry.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity; low-Ev features are only noted as 'often polysemantic on inspection'.
The existence of SAE-recoverable sparse features in the VLM is assumed, not tested. There is no measure of how features spread across neurons.
Completeness, stability and canonicity are not tested; the authors note SAEs are not a complete decomposition.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Table 1 values differ from Table 2 for features 27061, 23874 and 17873 (VSR accuracy and ∆Ctrl). The record says Table 1 duplicates Table 2.
Decoder-cosine alignment between base and adapted SAEs by layer and regime (text-only aligned; image/full rotate in early layers; random near zero).
missing.versions: none (possibly relevant to V5 stability across fine-tuning, but not framed as such)

record.verdict_notes: The SAE is the study's instrument; superposition is mentioned only as background (Sec. 3.2). The reader's V4 'supports' label rests on selection statistics and cherry-picked feature ablations, so I dropped it. Seed counts and uncertainty are not reported. Several random-control effects reach 1–2.7 pp, which weakens the specificity claim.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, excess sparse features, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions by feature importance.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for other reasons or are evidence of superposition.
The study examines SAE-recovered features in one multimodal model, not feature distribution across neurons in a range of LLMs or models generally.
Completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features is not empirically tested.
The study does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: LLaVA-More (LLaMA-3.1-8B backbone)
rows.operation_detail: Orthogonally removed the target SAE decoder direction from the residual stream at text-token positions
rows.uncertainty: averaged over seeds; error bars not stated
rows.note: The authors interpret large negative VSR accuracy deltas as spatially specific functional involvement.
rows.check: VSR accuracy drops from ablating hand-selected 'top' spatial features show these features' functional role in spatial reasoning. That bears on multimodal adaptation, not on superposition or V4's claim about feature distribution.
